source_doubts.where: Section 5, proof of Corollary 5.1 (uniformly bounded non-unitarizable representations)
source_doubts.problem: The whole proof is a citation to a companion theorem whose statement is not reproduced. To give the corollary from countability and nonamenability alone, that theorem would have to produce, for every countable nonamenable group and every epsilon>0, a non-unitarizable representation with bound 1+epsilon. That is a strong form of Dixmier's unitarizability problem, which is open in the established literature. The corollary cannot be checked from the manuscript. The same one-line proof is in the source.

source_doubts.where: Section 5, proof of Corollary 5.2 (percolation on Cayley graphs of F)
source_doubts.quote:
Apply the companion result \cite[Corollary~1.2]{OpenAIPercolation2026} to
$F$, nonamenable by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
source_doubts.problem: The proof is a bare citation to a companion result not reproduced in the manuscript. The conclusions (finite L2 operator norm at p_c, p_c < p_{2->2} <= p_u, and infinitely many infinite clusters throughout (p_c,p_u)) for every finite symmetric generating set of a nonamenable group amount to the Benjamini-Schramm p_c<p_u conjecture and its L2 strengthening, which are known only for special classes of graphs or generating sets. The corollary cannot be verified from the manuscript. The same one-line proof is in the source.

unverified_marks.where: End of Section 5 (Consequences), after the proof of Corollary 5.2
unverified_marks.concern: Both corollaries are one-line applications of companion theorems whose statements are not reproduced and could not be checked; the general statements they would need (non-unitarizable representations with bound 1+epsilon for every countable nonamenable group; the stated percolation conclusions for every Cayley graph of a nonamenable group) are not established in the earlier literature.
